# PICO gate — excluded works review

**Question this file answers:** the widened verb gate would newly run on six
benefit-shaped corpora and exclude 52 of 138 works. Are those exclusions the
gate working, or the gate misfiring?

**Data source:** `testdata/corpora_full/` — the untruncated re-export
(2026-07-25, see `corpora_full/README_export.md`). Every number here was
computed on complete abstracts, so none of it is a truncation artifact.

**Generated by:** `internal/scengine/pico_excluded_test.go`
(`go test ./internal/scengine/ -run TestPICOExcluded -v`). Re-runnable.

---

## ⚠️ How to read this file

Two kinds of statement appear below, and they are **not** the same kind of thing.

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔵 **MEASURED** | Title, year, citation count, which side of the claim failed to match, stance label, whether an abstract exists. Produced by code, reproducible by re-running the test. |
| 🟡 **JUDGED** | The (A)/(B)/(C) classification and its rationale. **This is Claude's editorial opinion**, formed by reading titles and abstract snippets. It is not a measurement, it was not validated against a domain expert, and it is the part most likely to be wrong. |

Every table below has both. The columns are labelled. When in doubt, trust the
🔵 columns and re-judge the 🟡 ones yourself.

Classification key:
- **(A) CORRECT** — the paper genuinely is not about this claim
- **(B) WRONG** — the paper is on-topic; the tokenizer failed to recognize it
- **(C) BORDERLINE** — arguable either way

Two thirds of exclusions fail on the **intervention** side — the paper never
names the thing the claim is about.

### ⚠️ Confounder: works with no abstract at all

| corpus | excluded | of those, no abstract | share | corpus-wide base rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| saffron | 5 | 0 | 0% | 1/12 (8%) |
| melatonin | 8 | 1 | 12% | 1/19 (5%) |
| meditation | 2 | 2 | 100% | 5/10 (50%) |
| omega3 | 30 | 10 | 33% | 15/62 (24%) |
| vitamind | 5 | 3 | 60% | 7/26 (27%) |
| probiotics | 2 | 2 | 100% | 4/9 (44%) |
| **TOTAL** | **52** | **18** | **35%** | **33/138 (24%)** |

**A work with no abstract is judged on its title alone.** Such works are
over-represented among exclusions (35% vs a 24% base rate) — roughly 1.5× more
likely to be dropped. This is a distinct failure mode from any tokenizer
weakness, and it is not fixed by widening the verb list or by a synonym table.

## saffron — 5 of 12 excluded

🔵 claim `"saffron extract reduces symptoms of mild depression"` → iv `[saffr extra]` out `[sympt mild depre]`

| 🔵 cites | 🔵 year | 🔵 title | 🔵 missing | 🔵 stance | 🟡 verdict | 🟡 rationale |
|---:|---:|---|---|---|:---:|---|
| 324 | 2022 | Tryptophan Metabolism in Depression: A Narrative Review with a Focus on Serotonin and Kynurenine Pathways | intervention | inconclusive | **A** | Depression neurobiology. Saffron is never mentioned; it is not evidence about saffron. |
| 242 | 2015 | Herbal Medicine for Anxiety, Depression and Insomnia | intervention | supporting | **C** | Abstract: *"Herb alone, as well as herbal formula, is commonly prescribed for the therapies of mental illnesses."* Saffron is a herbal antidepressant, so this review plausibly covers it — but it never names saffron, so the gate cannot know. |
| 174 | 2019 | Traditional and Modern Uses of Saffron (Crocus Sativus) | outcome | inconclusive | **A** | About saffron, but never names depression or symptoms. A general uses review is not evidence for this specific claim. |
| 145 | 2019 | Saffron: The Golden Spice with Therapeutic Properties on Digestive Diseases | outcome | inconclusive | **A** | Different outcome entirely (digestive disease). |
| 77 | 2014 | The ocular hypotensive effect of saffron extract in primary open angle glaucoma: a pilot study | outcome | inconclusive | **A** | Different outcome entirely (glaucoma). |

🟡 **4 correct, 1 borderline, 0 wrong.**

## melatonin — 8 of 19 excluded

🔵 claim `"melatonin supplementation improves sleep quality in shift workers"` → iv `[melat suppl]` out `[sleep quali shift worke]`

| 🔵 cites | 🔵 year | 🔵 title | 🔵 missing | 🔵 stance | 🟡 verdict | 🟡 rationale |
|---:|---:|---|---|---|:---:|---|
| 919 | 1995 | The Role of Actigraphy in the Evaluation of Sleep Disorders | intervention | supporting | **A** | Measurement methodology. No intervention studied at all. |
| 532 | 2015 | Sleep, circadian rhythms, and the pathogenesis of Alzheimer Disease | intervention | supporting | **A** | Alzheimer pathogenesis. No melatonin, no supplementation. |
| 411 | 2010 | Shift work, sleep, and sleepiness - differences between shift schedules and systems | intervention | supporting | **A** | Describes the population and the problem, but studies no intervention. |
| 379 | 2022 | Sleep Quality: A Narrative Review on Nutrition, Stimulants, and Physical Activity as Important Factors | intervention | supporting | **A** | Names three other factors; melatonin is not among them. |
| 308 | 2015 | The impact of sleep disorders on glucose metabolism: endocrine and molecular mechanisms | intervention | inconclusive | **A** | Glucose metabolism. Wrong direction and wrong intervention. |
| 268 | 2010 | Sleep and Metabolism: An Overview | intervention | supporting | **A** | Metabolism, no intervention. |
| 256 | 2016 | Increased Melatonin Signaling Is a Risk Factor for Type 2 Diabetes | outcome | supporting | **A** | Melatonin, but the outcome is diabetes — and it is endogenous signalling, not supplementation. |

🔵 ⚠️ 10 of the 30 have no abstract. Note also that the claim's `"3"` is dropped
by the 4-character token floor, so the intervention side is the single stem
`omega` — the same single-character weakness as vitamin D.

### 🔵 Missing the outcome (6 works)

| 🔵 cites | 🔵 year | 🔵 title | 🔵 stance | 🟡 verdict | 🟡 rationale |
|---:|---:|---|---|:---:|---|
| 1360 | 2017 | Omega-3 fatty acids and inflammatory processes: from molecules to man | supporting | **A** | Inflammation, not a cardiovascular endpoint. |
| 1332 | 2012 | Omega‐3 polyunsaturated fatty acids and inflammatory processes: nutrition or pharmacology? | supporting | **A** | Inflammation. (Note the U+2010 hyphen in the title — irrelevant to the gate, whose tokens are single alphanumeric runs.) |
| 734 | 2017 | Impact of Omega-3 Fatty Acids on the Gut Microbiota | supporting | **A** | Gut microbiota endpoint. |
| 573 | 2011 | Omega-3 supplementation and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: systematic review and meta-analysis | inconclusive | **A** | Liver endpoint. |
| 468 | 2016 | Metabolism and functional effects of plant-derived omega-3 fatty acids in humans | inconclusive | **C** | Mechanistic metabolism paper; "functional effects" may include cardiovascular ones, but none is named. No abstract. |
| **224** | 2012 | **Effect of omega-3 fatty acids supplementation on endothelial function: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials** | inconclusive | **B** | **Endothelial function is a cardiovascular outcome.** The outcome tokens `[cardi, healt]` have no synonym for it. A meta-analysis of RCTs — the top of the evidence pyramid — dropped on outcome vocabulary. |

🟡 **omega3 total: 24 correct, 3 borderline, 3 wrong.**

The headline is not the three misses — it is that **21 of the 24
intervention-side exclusions are cardiology guidelines, nutrition reviews and
unrelated biology that never mention omega-3 at all.** OpenAlex's relevance
search returned them because they match "cardiovascular health"; the PICO gate
is doing precisely the job it was built for.

## vitamind — 5 of 26 excluded

🔵 claim `"vitamin D reduces respiratory infections"` → iv `[vitam]` out `[respi infec]`
🔵 All five fail on the **outcome** side. 3 of 5 have no abstract.

| 🔵 cites | 🔵 year | 🔵 title | 🔵 stance | 🟡 verdict | 🟡 rationale |
|---:|---:|---|---|:---:|---|
| 1780 | 2008 | Vitamin D and Human Health: Lessons from Vitamin D Receptor Null Mice | supporting | **A** | Doubly excludable: no respiratory outcome, **and it is a mouse study** — the species gate should have removed it first. |
| 1402 | 2020 | Vitamin D deficiency 2.0: an update on the current status worldwide | inconclusive | **A** | Prevalence epidemiology, no clinical outcome. |
| 1297 | 2013 | Vitamin D for Health: A Global Perspective | inconclusive | **A** | Broad perspective piece. |
| 1136 | 2013 | Vitamin D and Immune Function | supporting | **C** | Abstract: *"vitamin D also promotes a more tolerogenic immunological status."* Immune function is the mechanism by which vitamin D would affect respiratory infection, so this is mechanistically upstream of the claim — but it names no respiratory endpoint. |
| 555 | 2011 | The VITamin D and OmegA-3 TriaL (VITAL): Rationale and design … for the primary prevention of cancer and cardiovascular disease | supporting | **A** | Trial-design paper whose stated endpoints are cancer and CVD, not respiratory infection. |

🟡 **4 correct, 1 borderline, 0 wrong.**

Note the separate, already-documented defect: the intervention token is `vitam`,
which matches vitamin C papers too. That produces **false inclusions**, which
this file (about exclusions) does not show. See `TestPICOImpactVitaminD`.

## 🟡 JUDGED — Overall verdict

| classification | count | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **(A) CORRECT** — genuinely off-claim | **42** | **81%** |
| **(B) WRONG** — on-topic, tokenizer failed | **4** | **8%** |
| **(C) BORDERLINE** | **6** | **11%** |
| total | 52 | |

The four (B) cases:

1. omega3 — *HEALTH BENEFITS OF DOCOSAHEXAENOIC ACID (DHA)* — intervention synonym
2. omega3 — *(n-3) Fatty Acids and Cardiovascular Health: EPA and DHA* — intervention synonym
3. omega3 — *Effect of omega-3 … on endothelial function: meta-analysis of RCTs* — outcome synonym
4. probiotics — *The pros, cons, and many unknowns of probiotics* — no abstract, title too short to carry both sides

## 🔵 MEASURED — The omega-3 synonym question

Of the **30** works excluded from omega3:

| measure | count |
|---|---:|
| whose **title** names an omega-3 synonym | **3 of 30** |
| whose **title or abstract** names one | **6 of 30** |

Per synonym (title or abstract):

| synonym | hits |
|---|---:|
| fish oil | 2 |
| EPA / eicosapentaenoic | 3 |
| DHA / docosahexaenoic | 4 |
| n-3 | 4 |
| PUFA | 2 |
| polyunsaturated | 3 |

### 🟡 JUDGED — what that means

**The synonym table is a smaller win than expected.** Of the 6 works that name a
synonym, **4 already match `omega` anyway** and are excluded on the *outcome*
side — a synonym table for the intervention would not save them. Only **2** are
excluded *because* the intervention synonym was invisible (the DHA paper and the
(n-3) EPA/DHA paper).

So an intervention synonym table would recover **2 of 30 omega3 exclusions
(7%)**, or **2 of 52 across all six corpora (4%)**.

---

## 🟡 JUDGED — Recommendation

**1. Widening the verb gate looks safe to ship.** 81% of the exclusions it
newly produces are correct, 8% are wrong, and the one control corpus
(`meditation`) loses no genuinely on-topic study — its riskiest case turned out
to be a truncation artifact that the full re-export cleared. The corpora it
would newly filter are visibly full of topic-adjacent noise that the gate
removes well (melatonin 8/8 correct; omega3's 21 cardiology guidelines).

**2. The synonym table is *not* the higher-priority fix.** The hypothesis that
it would be a large win is not supported: measured yield is 2 of 52 exclusions.
Worth doing eventually, cheap to do, but it is not what is holding the gate back.

**3. The largest identified weakness is missing abstracts, not vocabulary.**
24% of works in these corpora arrive with no abstract, and they make up 35% of
exclusions — over-represented by ~1.5×. Both remaining (B)-class errors outside
the two omega-3 synonym cases trace to a title-only judgment. Sourcing abstracts
for those works (Crossref or PubMed already sit in this CLI's source layer) would
address more excluded-work error than a synonym table, and would improve stance
classification at the same time.

**4. Two known defects this file does not cover.** The `vitam` token admits
vitamin C papers (false *inclusions*, see `TestPICOImpactVitaminD`), and the
4-character token floor discards `"D"` and `"3"` from `"vitamin D"` and
`"omega-3"`. Both are separate from anything measured here.
